description: What this shows: Transaction queue depth and capacity, fee-escalation levels, and load-factor breakdown that together set the minimum fee to enter the open ledger.  —  Use it to: Understand why the minimum transaction fee is rising and how full the open ledger and queue are.

panels.title: Transaction Queue Depth
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Transactions currently waiting in the transaction queue versus the queue's maximum capacity.*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge readings of current queue count and configured max size.*

###### Reading it:
*Queue depth well below capacity is normal; depth approaching capacity means the node is saturating.*

###### Healthy range:
*Depth near 0 in quiet periods; workload-dependent under load.*

###### Watch for:
*Depth pinned at capacity for sustained periods, which signals demand exceeding throughput or a fee-spam burst.*

###### Keywords:
- **Transaction queue (TxQ)** — holds transactions that meet local cost but not the open-ledger cost, to include in a later ledger.

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerTxqGauge`

###### References:
[Transaction queue (TxQ)](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/transactions/transaction-queue) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#transaction-queue-txq)

panels.title: Transactions Per Ledger
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Transactions already placed in the current open ledger versus the expected per-ledger target.*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge readings of in-ledger count and the target count that governs fee escalation.*

###### Reading it:
*Staying at or below the expected target is normal; exceeding it triggers open-ledger fee escalation.*

###### Healthy range:
*At or under the expected per-ledger target.*

###### Watch for:
*In-ledger count persistently above target, indicating sustained congestion pushing fees up.*

###### Keywords:
- **Open ledger** — the temporary workspace ledger where incoming transactions are provisionally applied before a close.
- **In-ledger vs target count** — transactions already in the open ledger versus the soft target that triggers fee escalation.
- **Fee escalation** — the exponential rise in the open-ledger cost once the ledger exceeds its soft transaction target.

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerTxqGauge`

###### References:
[Open ledger](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/ledgers/open-closed-validated-ledgers) · [In-ledger vs target count](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/transactions/transaction-cost#open-ledger-cost) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#open-ledger)

panels.title: Fee Escalation Levels
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The fee levels that govern queue admission: reference (baseline), minimum processing, median, and open-ledger levels.*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge readings of each fee level, shown on a log scale.*

###### Reading it:
*Open-ledger level near the reference level means cheap entry; a large gap above reference means escalation is active.*

###### Healthy range:
*Open-ledger level at or near reference during normal traffic.*

###### Watch for:
*Open-ledger level spiking far above reference, the hallmark of congestion or a fee-bidding war.*

###### Keywords:
- **Queue admission rejection** — a transaction refused entry to the queue, e.g. queue_full when the queue is at capacity.
- **Fee levels** — cost thresholds governing queue admission: reference (baseline), minimum, median, and open-ledger.
- **Open ledger** — the temporary workspace ledger where incoming transactions are provisionally applied before a close.
- **Fee escalation** — the exponential rise in the open-ledger cost once the ledger exceeds its soft transaction target.

[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

`registerTxqGauge`

panels.title: Load Factor Breakdown
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The combined load factor and its server, fee-escalation, and fee-queue contributors as unitless fee multipliers (1.0 = no load).*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge readings of each load-factor component.*

###### Reading it:
*Values at 1.0 mean base fees; higher values raise the fee to transact.*

###### Healthy range:
*Around 1.0 under normal conditions.*

###### Watch for:
*Combined factor climbing well above 1.0, showing the node is charging premium fees due to congestion or overload.*

###### Keywords:
- **Load factor** — a unitless multiplier (1.0 = no load) that scales the base transaction cost as the node comes under load.
- **Fee escalation** — the exponential rise in the open-ledger cost once the ledger exceeds its soft transaction target.
- **Transaction cost** — the XRP a transaction destroys to be processed; scales up with load to deter spam.

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerLoadFactorGauge`

###### References:
[Load factor](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/transactions/transaction-cost#local-load-cost) · [Fee escalation](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/transactions/transaction-cost#open-ledger-cost) · [Transaction cost](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/transactions/transaction-cost) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#load-factor)

panels.title: Load Factor Components
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The individual load-factor inputs, local server load, network load, and cluster load, as unitless multipliers.*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge readings of each component.*

###### Reading it:
*All at 1.0 means no load pressure from any source; a raised component identifies where load originates.*

###### Healthy range:
*Around 1.0 for each component.*

###### Watch for:
*A single component rising sharply, which pinpoints whether the pressure is local, network-wide, or cluster-driven.*

###### Keywords:
- **Load factor** — a unitless multiplier (1.0 = no load) that scales the base transaction cost as the node comes under load.
- **Cluster** — a group of trusted co-operated nodes that share load information and skip some verification.

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerLoadFactorGauge`

###### References:
[Load factor](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/transactions/transaction-cost#local-load-cost) · [Cluster](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/networks-and-servers/clustering) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#load-factor)

panels.title: Queue Abandonment Rate (Expired)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Transactions dropped from the queue because their last-ledger deadline passed before they could be included.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of the cumulative expired-transaction counter over the dashboard's rate interval.*

###### Reading it:
*Near zero is healthy; a rising rate means submitters under-bid the escalating fee and their transactions timed out.*

###### Healthy range:
*Near 0 expirations per second.*

###### Watch for:
*Sustained expiry rate, a demand-frustration signal often coinciding with fee spikes or spam that crowds out honest traffic.*

###### Keywords:
- **Queue admission rejection** — a transaction refused entry to the queue, e.g. queue_full when the queue is at capacity.
- **Queue expiry / abandonment** — removing a queued transaction whose LastLedgerSequence deadline passed before inclusion.
- **Fee escalation** — the exponential rise in the open-ledger cost once the ledger exceeds its soft transaction target.

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`incrementTxqExpired (caller TxQ.cpp)`

###### References:
[Queue admission rejection](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/transactions/transaction-queue) · [Queue expiry / abandonment](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/transactions/reliable-transaction-submission) · [Fee escalation](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/transactions/transaction-cost#open-ledger-cost) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#queue-admission-rejection)

panels.title: Queue Admission Rejections (Dropped)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Transactions refused entry to the queue, broken down by reason such as queue_full.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of the cumulative dropped-transaction counter over the dashboard's rate interval, split by reason.*

###### Reading it:
*Near zero is healthy; queue_full rejections mean the queue is at capacity and applying backpressure.*

###### Healthy range:
*Near 0 rejections per second.*

###### Watch for:
*A burst of queue_full drops, distinct from expiry, indicating the node is being flooded faster than it can drain.*

###### Keywords:
- **Queue admission rejection** — a transaction refused entry to the queue, e.g. queue_full when the queue is at capacity.

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`incrementTxqDropped (caller TxQ.cpp)`

###### References:
[Queue admission rejection](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/transactions/transaction-queue) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#queue-admission-rejection)
